<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>Circle</title>
  <style>
    *,
    *::before,
    *::after {
      box-sizing: border-box;
      margin: 0;
      padding: 0;
    }

    html,
    body {
      height: 100%;
    }

    body {
      display: flex;
      justify-content: center;
      align-items: center;
      min-height: 100dvh;
      background: #f7f7f5;
      color: #1a1a1a;
    }

    svg {
      display: block;
      width: min(400px, 80vmin);
      height: auto;
      aspect-ratio: 1 / 1;
    }

    @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
      body {
        background: #121212;
        color: #ededed;
      }
    }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <svg id="ae683f770" viewBox="0 0 400 400" role="img" aria-labelledby="circle-title">
    <title id="circle-title">A solid circle</title>
    <circle cx="200" cy="200" r="200" fill="currentColor"/>
  </svg>
</body>
</html>

content.text:
Updated `0.html`. It was a bare page centering a 400px black circle, so I kept that intent and fixed the rough edges:

- **No stray scrollbars.** Replaced `width: 100vw` with normal full-height sizing, which avoids the horizontal scrollbar that 100vw causes when a vertical scrollbar is present. Added a box-sizing reset.
- **Responsive circle.** The SVG now shrinks on small screens instead of overflowing, capped at 400px.
- **Accessibility.** The SVG has an image role and a title, and the page title is now descriptive instead of a random hash.
- **Theming.** The circle uses the text color, with a light background by default and a dark variant via `prefers-color-scheme`.

The original ID on the SVG is preserved in case anything references it.
